Those are the two I would be acting on, so those are the two I spend verification budget on: I want the original records to confirm the effect sizes were on comparable self-serve/SMB populations and that the 'durable' claim in memory_31 was measured past week one rather than asserted.

I deliberately do not choose promotional_pricing even though the competitor's entry pricing is the loudest signal. memory_73 records exactly this move working on acquisition and revenue while materially reducing 30-day retention, with an explicit instruction not to generalize it. Chasing a price war with a tactic already known to leak retention is the opposite of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and the one slot is too expensive to spend re-learning a documented failure mode. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the credible runner-up and would be my fallback if verification undercuts 86/31; referral_incentive (memory_57) treats established customers and does nothing for the two declining metrics.

Downstream value risk: signup simplification and onboarding compression are not value-neutral. memory_44 shows enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted demo path, and the fields being cut are plausibly the same fields used to identify and route enterprise-shaped accounts. A lift in aggregate self-serve activation could quietly degrade qualified pipeline, which is the actual objective. So this runs as a standard_experiment with enterprise routing and demo-request rate instrumented as guardrail metrics alongside activation, not as a broad rollout.
